$comment: Curated manifest of public-domain source documents for the corpus. Every entry states its rights basis, because 'found on a government site' is not a rights determination. Fetch with tools/acquire.py; the tool refuses hosts that are not on its allowlist and names freechecklists.net in its denylist with the reason.

source.title: Airplane Flying Handbook, Chapter 2: Ground Operations
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service

documents.notes: Text extracts cleanly with PyMuPDF; no OCR needed. Generic single-engine procedures, not type-specific. Already transcribed as examples/faa-generic-sep-ground-operations.ocl.json.

source.title: Flight Handbook, USAF Series T-34A Aircraft

documents.notes: High-value: the T-34 is flown by civilians today in the experimental/limited category, and the handbook carries a full CONDENSED CHECK LIST for normal and emergency procedures. OCR CAVEAT, measured rather than assumed: 12 of 164 pages extract as mojibake (>15% non-ASCII), e.g. '"AAO - SUMS PY "FZ' where the page reads '24. All switches - OFF.' Those pages are 180 degrees inverted, and three of them (49, 51, 53) sit inside the block marked 'CUT ON LINE' (pages 48-61). The cause is the original print design, not the scan: the condensed checklist is a cut-out card whose alternating panels are printed upside down so they read correctly once folded. The consequence for the pipeline is pointed -- the least reliably OCR'd pages are exactly the ones containing the checklist. Rotation detection must be a pipeline stage, and it must be per page rather than per document, since /Rotate is 0 on all 164 pages.

source.title: 28 Day NASR Subscription (airports, runways, frequencies, navaids)
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration

documents.notes: 248 MB subscriber zip containing an inner CSV_Data bundle; parse that rather than the 232 MB fixed-width APT.txt. Ingest with tools/airports.py, which emits a lean search index plus 35 detail shards. NOT COMMITTED: the ingested output is ~30 MB, so data/ is gitignored and the site build generates airport pages only when the data is present. Re-ingest every 28 days -- the URL embeds the AIRAC effective date, and the effective date is carried through into cycle.json and shown on every airport page, because a stale frequency is worse than no frequency.

source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration

documents.notes: The core airframe maintenance and repair reference, and the single most useful public-domain troubleshooting document for this audience. Full text is indexable because it is a US Government work.

source.title: Powered Parachute Flying Handbook
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service

documents.notes: The authoritative FAA handbook for powered parachute pilots. 161 pages covering certification, aerodynamics, systems, preflight inspection, ground ops, takeoff, normal flight, emergency procedures. Chapter 12 covers emergency situations including engine failure on climbout, engine failure in flight, in-flight fire, and rollover. Chapter 5 covers the preflight checklist and Chapter 7 covers the before-takeoff check. Note: the FAA aviation handbooks page links to this document at /sites/faa.gov/files/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/powered_parachute_handbook.pdf — the document identifies itself as FAA-H-8083-12A (2007) internally; the B revision mentioned in user notes may refer to a later revision not yet on the FAA site.

source.title: Glider Flying Handbook
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service

documents.notes: The complete FAA glider flying handbook. Covers glider systems, aerodynamics, preflight inspection, ground handling, launches (aerotow and ground-tow), soaring techniques, navigation, and emergency procedures. The FAA glider handbook page offers the book as individual chapter PDFs; the consolidated single-file PDF is at /sites/faa.gov/files/Glider-Flying-Handbook.pdf.

source.title: Rotorcraft Flying Handbook
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service

documents.notes: The FAA rotorcraft flying handbook covering helicopters and gyroplanes. Includes preflight inspection procedures, engine starting, hover taxi, takeoff, autorotation, and emergency procedures. Note: an updated 'B' revision may exist; this is the version currently linked from the FAA aviation handbooks page at /sites/faa.gov/files/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/faa-h-8083-21.pdf.

source.title: Weight-Shift Control Aircraft Flying Handbook
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, Flight Standards Service

documents.notes: The FAA weight-shift control (trike/microlight) flying handbook. WSC aircraft use a hang-glider wing with a trike unit below. Covers preflight inspection, engine start, ground roll, takeoff, normal flight maneuvers, and emergency procedures. PDF at /sites/faa.gov/files/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/FAA-H-8083-5.pdf.

discovery_recipes.$comment: Search patterns that surface public-domain aircraft documentation. Run with `tools/acquire.py discover "<query>"`. Recorded because finding these took longer than fetching them, and because the useful phrasings are not obvious.
notes: US military flight manuals are the richest type-specific public-domain lane, and many cover aircraft civilians fly today: T-34, T-6/SNJ, T-28, L-19/O-1, L-17, PT-series.
Check authorship before claiming 17 USC 105. Contractor-authored technical data is not automatically a US Government work even when it carries a military document number.

FAA Type Certificate Data Sheets (drs.faa.gov) are US Government works containing certificated limitations and placards for civil types. They are not checklists, but they are an authoritative public-domain source for the numeric limitations that transcribed checklists must not invent. Worth mining once the checklist structure is settled.

freechecklists.net may be browsed as an index to learn which documents exist for which types -- facts about what exists are not protected -- but its files must not be copied. See docs/05-product-and-sourcing.md section 2.
